code:
# Lab 09 - pins and PWM: a dimmer on the edge connector.
# Inputs:  touch logo = on/off, A/B = brightness level, touch pin0 = boost.
# Outputs: pin1 = on/off indicator (digital), pin2 = LED brightness (PWM).
from microbit import *

LEVELS = 4                      # brightness steps 0..LEVELS
PERIOD_MS = 20                  # PWM period: 20 ms = 50 Hz
pin2.set_analog_period(PERIOD_MS)


def duty_for(level):
    # write_analog takes 0 (0 % duty) .. 1023 (100 % duty)
    return level * 1023 // LEVELS


def new_state():
    return {"on": False, "level": 2, "logo_was": False, "last": None}


def step(state):
    # edge detect: is_touched() is a level ("touched now"), we want the moment it starts
    touched = pin_logo.is_touched()
    if touched and not state["logo_was"]:
        state["on"] = not state["on"]
    state["logo_was"] = touched
    if button_a.was_pressed():
        state["level"] = min(LEVELS, state["level"] + 1)
    if button_b.was_pressed():
        state["level"] = max(0, state["level"] - 1)
    boost = pin0.is_touched()   # pin0..2 touch is resistive by default (touch GND too)
    duty = 0
    if state["on"]:
        duty = 1023 if boost else duty_for(state["level"])
    pin1.write_digital(1 if state["on"] else 0)    # digital output: 0 V or 3.3 V
    pin2.write_analog(duty)                        # PWM output: average voltage = duty/1023 * 3.3 V
    report = (state["on"], state["level"], duty)
    if report != state["last"]:                    # print only changes
        print("on={},level={},duty={}".format(int(state["on"]), state["level"], duty))
        state["last"] = report
    return duty


def main():
    print("logo = on/off, A/B = level, pin0 = boost")
    state = new_state()
    while True:
        step(state)
        sleep(50)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

codeWalkthrough.title: pin2.set_analog_period(PERIOD_MS)
codeWalkthrough.detail: PWM period 20 ms (50 Hz). Minimum 1 ms (or 256 µs with the microseconds call).

codeWalkthrough.title: if touched and not state['logo_was']
codeWalkthrough.detail: Edge detection: toggle only when touch starts, not every poll while held.

codeWalkthrough.title: pin1.write_digital(...) / pin2.write_analog(duty)
codeWalkthrough.detail: Digital: 0 or 1. PWM: 0..1023, values outside raise ValueError.

codeWalkthrough.title: if report != state['last']
codeWalkthrough.detail: Print only changes so serial stays readable at a 50 ms poll.

code:
# Lab 10 - an external temperature sensor over I2C (TMP102 register map).
# Wiring on a real board: SCL -> pin19, SDA -> pin20, GND, 3V; ADD0 -> GND.
# The browser simulator has NO I2C devices: expect "no device" there.
# Unit tests attach a simulated TMP102 (labs/sim_stub/i2c_devices.py).
from microbit import *

ADDR = 0x48            # 7-bit address (TMP102 with ADD0 to GND)
REG_TEMP = 0x00        # pointer register values: temperature (read-only)
REG_CONFIG = 0x01      # configuration, power-up value 0x60A0
LSB_C = 0.0625         # 12-bit result: one step = 0.0625 C


def decode_temp(msb, lsb):
    # 12-bit two's complement, left-justified: MSB holds bits 11..4, LSB bits 3..0
    raw = (msb << 4) | (lsb >> 4)
    if raw & 0x800:                      # sign bit set -> negative temperature
        raw -= 4096
    return raw * LSB_C


def read_register(reg, n=2):
    i2c.write(ADDR, bytes([reg]))        # 1) set the pointer register
    return i2c.read(ADDR, n)             # 2) read n bytes, most significant first


def read_temp_c():
    data = read_register(REG_TEMP)
    return decode_temp(data[0], data[1])


def step():
    # an I2C error is an OSError; 19 (ENODEV) = nothing answered at ADDR
    try:
        t = read_temp_c()
    except OSError as e:
        print("i2c: no device at {} (errno {})".format(hex(ADDR), e.args[0]))
        display.show(Image.NO, wait=False)
        return None
    print("temp_c={:.2f}".format(t))
    display.show(Image.YES if t < 30 else Image.ANGRY, wait=False)
    return t


def main():
    print("scan:", [hex(a) for a in i2c.scan()])   # which addresses answer?
    while True:
        step()
        sleep(1000)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

codeWalkthrough.detail: Two's complement: top bit set means negative.

title: A game as a state machine
description: Catch-the-dot with states idle/play/over, events from buttons, shake and time, and a testable transition table.
outcome: You can structure an interactive program as a state machine and test every transition.
environment: As L100 lesson 1 (Python Editor v3 + V2 simulator; Python 3.12 + labs/sim_stub; CI Node 24 + Playwright 1.64.1). No new packages; the stub adds radio, log, pins, i2c.
overview: One explicit state plus a (state, event) table replaces tangled flags; time is just another event.

glossary.meaning: Where the program is: idle, play or over.
Something that happened: a, shake, timeout.

concepts: Events from inputs and the clock.
